answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to stake a small, time-locked bond tied to verifiable work history, so spinning up fake identities becomes expensive instead of free. Like a falcon proving its hunting skill before joining the flock, an agent earns reputation only through completed, attested tasks that build a record no single actor can forge overnight. Old credentials should not be kept as a relic to worship blindly; they decay unless refreshed by honest work, and trust should flow like a river, continuously, from peers who actually transacted with the agent.
